title.zh: 卷十七 列傳第十一: 王沖 王通 袁敬
title.en: Volume 17: Wang Chong; Wang Tong; Yuan Jing
title.raw: 卷十七 列傳第十一: 王沖 王通 袁敬 Volume 17: Wang Chong; Wang Tong; Yuan Jing

sentences.zh: 陳書卷十七

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 17
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 17

sentences.zh: 列傳第十一

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Eleven
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Part Eleven

sentences.zh: 王沖 王通弟勱 袁敬兄子樞

translations.literal: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu

sentences.zh: 王沖字長深，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Chong, styled Changshen, was a native of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong, styled Changshen, was a native of Linyi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 祖僧衍，齊侍中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sengyan was Palace Attendant of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengyan had been palace attendant of Qi.

sentences.zh: 父茂璋，梁給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Maozhang was Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate in Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Maozhang was an attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate under Liang.

sentences.zh: 沖母，梁武帝妹新安穆公主，卒於齊世，武帝以沖偏孤，深所鍾愛。

translations.literal: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, sister of Emperor Wu of Liang; she died in Qi times, and the Emperor, because Chong was a lone orphan, cherished him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, a sister of Emperor Wu of Liang. She died in Qi times, and the emperor, finding Chong a fatherless child, doted on him.

sentences.zh: 年十八，起家梁祕書郎。

translations.literal: At eighteen he began his career as Secretary of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he entered service as a secretary of Liang.

sentences.zh: 尋為永嘉太守。

translations.literal: Soon he became Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made administrator of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 入為太子舍人，以父憂去職。

translations.literal: He entered court as Mentor to the Heir Apparent and left office on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as mentor to the heir apparent and resigned when his father died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除太尉臨川王府外兵參軍、東宮領直。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed External Military Aide on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan in the Grand Marshal's office and Leader of Direct Service in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was named external military aide on the Prince of Linchuan's staff in the Grand Marshal's office and leader of direct service in the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子洗馬、中舍人。

translations.literal: He rose through Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent and Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to be grand mentor to the heir apparent and attendant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 出為招遠將軍、衡陽內史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Recruits the Distant and Interior Magistrate of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as General Who Recruits the Distant and interior magistrate of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 遷武威將軍、安成嗣王長史、長沙內史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Martial Prestige, Chief Clerk to the Heir of the Princedom of Ancheng, and Interior Magistrate of Changsha, his rank as general unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of Martial Prestige, chief clerk to the heir of Ancheng, and interior magistrate of Changsha, retaining his general's title.

sentences.zh: 王薨於湘州，仍以沖監湘州事。

translations.literal: When the prince died in Xiangzhou, Chong was left to oversee Xiangzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince died at Xiangzhou, Chong was left to govern the province.

sentences.zh: 入為太子庶子。

translations.literal: He entered court as Household Supporter of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as household supporter of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 大同三年，以帝甥賜爵安東亭侯，[1]邑一百五十戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, as the emperor's sister's son he was enfeoffed Marquis of Andong ting, Editorial footnote marker 1. with a fief of one hundred fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong (537), as kin of the imperial house he was made Marquis of Andong, [1] with a fief of one hundred fifty households.

sentences.zh: 歷明威將軍、南郡太守、太子中庶子、侍中。

translations.literal: He served as General of Manifest Prestige, Administrator of Nan commandery, Household Supporter of the Heir Apparent, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of General of Manifest Prestige, administrator of Nan commandery, household supporter of the heir apparent, and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 出監吳郡，滿歲即真。

translations.literal: He went out to oversee Wu commandery; when his term ended he received the actual appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to oversee Wu commandery and, when his term ended, received the substantive appointment.

sentences.zh: 徵為通直散騎常侍，兼左民尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Regular Attendant of the Secretariat, concurrently Master of the Left for the People.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as regular attendant of the Secretariat and made concurrent master of the left for the people.

sentences.zh: 出為明威將軍、輕車當陽公府長史、江夏太守，行郢州事。

translations.literal: He went out as General of Manifest Prestige, Chief Clerk to the Prince of Dangyang, Administrator of Jiangxia, conducting office in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as General of Manifest Prestige, chief clerk to the Prince of Dangyang, administrator of Jiangxia, and acting governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷平西邵陵王長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk to the Prince of Shaoling, General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk to the Prince of Shaoling, General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 轉驃騎廬陵王長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk to the Prince of Luling, Grand General of Cavalry, and Administrator of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk to the Prince of Luling, grand general of cavalry, and administrator of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 王薨，行州府事。

translations.literal: When the prince died, he conducted the prefecture and princely establishment affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince died, he ran the prefecture and the princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝鎮荊州，為鎮西長史，將軍、太守如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang held Jingzhou, he was Chief Clerk to the Establishment Pacifying the West, general and administrator unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang held Jingzhou, he became chief clerk to the establishment pacifying the west, keeping his general's title and his post as administrator.

sentences.zh: 沖性和順，事上謹肅，習於法令，政在平理，佐藩两人，鮮有失德，雖無赫赫之譽，久而見思，由是推重，累居二千石。

translations.literal: Chong's nature was gentle and compliant; in serving superiors he was reverent; versed in statutes, his governance fair and orderly; as aide in two princely establishments he rarely failed in virtue; though he won no brilliant renown, over time men came to miss him—thus he was esteemed and repeatedly held office at the two-thousand-shi level.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was mild and obliging, reverent toward his superiors, and skilled in law; his rule was even-handed. Twice he served as an aide to princely establishments and scarcely stained his name. He won no dazzling fame, yet men remembered him long after—so he was held in esteem and repeatedly held governorships.

sentences.zh: 又曉音樂，習歌舞，善與人交，貴游之中，聲名藉甚。

translations.literal: He also understood music, was skilled in song and dance, and good at friendship; among the noble wanderers his fame was very great.
translations.idiomatic: He also knew music, excelled at song and dance, and made friends easily; among the great families his name rang far.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，梁元帝於荊州承制，沖求解南郡，以讓王僧辯，并獻女妓十人，以助軍賞。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan of Liang at Jingzhou assumed the provisional regime; Chong asked to be relieved of Nan commandery to yield it to Wang Sengbian, and also presented ten female entertainers as military reward.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion, when Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the provisional regime at Jingzhou, Chong asked to give up Nan commandery for Wang Sengbian and sent ten female entertainers as a gift toward the army's expenses.

sentences.zh: 元帝授持節、督衡桂成合四州諸軍事、雲麾將軍、衡州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuan appointed him Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs over the four prefectures Heng, Gui, Cheng, and He, General of the Clouded Pennon, and Inspector of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan made him bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs over Heng, Gui, Cheng, and He, General of the Clouded Pennon, and inspector of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 元帝第四子元良為湘州刺史，仍以沖行州事，領長沙內史。

translations.literal: Yuan's fourth son Yuanliang was Inspector of Xiangzhou; Chong again conducted the province, concurrently Interior Magistrate of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's fourth son Yuanliang was inspector of Xiangzhou; Chong again governed the province while serving as interior magistrate of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，授翊左將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, he was appointed General Who Assists the Left and Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing was suppressed, he was made General Who Assists the Left and intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 武陵王舉兵至峽口，王琳偏將陸納等據湘州應之，沖為納所拘。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wuling raised troops to the gorge mouth, Wang Lin's lieutenant Lu Na and others held Xiangzhou in response; Chong was detained by Na.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wuling marched to the gorge mouth, Wang Lin's lieutenant Lu Na and others seized Xiangzhou in support; Chong was held by Na.

sentences.zh: 納降，重授侍中、中權將軍，量置佐史，尹如故。

translations.literal: When Na surrendered, Chong was again appointed Palace Attendant and General of Central Authority, with aides and clerks as needed, Intendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Na surrendered, Chong was again made palace attendant and General of Central Authority, with aides and clerks as needed, and kept the intendant's post.

sentences.zh: 江陵陷，敬帝為太宰，承制以沖為左長史。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing of Liang as Grand Preceptor assumed the provisional regime and made Chong left chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing of Liang, acting as grand preceptor under the provisional regime, made Chong his left chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 紹泰中，累遷左光祿大夫、尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the Shaotai era he rose through Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the right.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shaotai era he rose from left grand master of the golden sigil to right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 遷左僕射、開府儀同三司，侍中、將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director, Opener of the Mansion Equal to the Three Dukes, Palace Attendant and general unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left vice director and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, retaining palace attendant and his general's title.

sentences.zh: 尋復領丹陽尹、南徐州大中正，給扶。

translations.literal: Soon he again headed Danyang as Intendant and Grand Arbiter of South Xuzhou, with support staff granted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he again headed Danyang as intendant and served as grand arbiter of South Xuzhou, with aides granted to support him.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，解尹，以本官領左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, he was relieved as Intendant; in his former office he headed Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, he left the intendant's post and, in his former rank, headed the left grand master of the golden sigil.

sentences.zh: 未拜，改領太子少傅。

translations.literal: Before he took up the appointment, he was changed to head Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Before he entered that office he was reassigned to head tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 文帝嗣位，解少傅，加特進、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he was relieved as Junior Tutor and given Supernumerary Privilege and Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he was relieved as junior tutor and given supernumerary privilege together with the left grand master of the golden sigil.

sentences.zh: 尋又以本官領丹陽尹，參撰律令。

translations.literal: Soon in his former office he again headed Danyang as Intendant and joined in compiling statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, in his former capacity, he again headed Danyang as intendant and took part in compiling statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，給親信十人。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was given ten trusted attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, he was granted ten trusted attendants.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖以沖前代舊臣，特申長幼之敬。

translations.literal: At first the Founder, because Chong was an old minister of the previous dynasty, specially showed him the respect due elder and younger.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Founder, treating Chong as a veteran of the old court, paid him the special courtesy owed between elder and younger.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，益加尊重，嘗從文帝幸司空徐度宅，宴筵之上，賜以几。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, respect increased; once he followed Emperor Wen on a visit to Minister of Works Xu Du's residence, and at the banquet the Emperor gave him an armrest.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, the honor grew; once, accompanying the emperor to Minister of Works Xu Du's house, he was given an armrest at the banquet.

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the honor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 光大元年薨，時年七十六。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangda he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangda (567) he died, aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、司空，諡曰元簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, posthumous name Yuancian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace attendant and minister of works, with the posthumous name Yuancian.

sentences.zh: 沖有子三十人。

translations.literal: Chong had thirty sons.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had thirty sons.

sentences.zh: 嵭致通官。

translations.literal: All reached regular office.
translations.idiomatic: All of them rose to regular office.

sentences.zh: 第十二子瑒，別有傳。

translations.literal: The twelfth son Yang has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth son, Yang, has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 王通字公達，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Tong, styled Gongda, was a native of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong, styled Gongda, was a native of Linyi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 祖份，梁左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fen was Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fen had been left grand master of the golden sigil under Liang.

sentences.zh: 父琳，司徒左長史。

translations.literal: His father Lin was Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lin was left chief clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: [2]琳，齊代娶梁武帝妹義興長公主，有子九人，嵭知名。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 2. Lin, in Qi times married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister Princess of Yixing long, had nine sons, and all became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 2. Lin, in Qi times, married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess of Yixing long; he had nine sons, all of whom won notice.

sentences.zh: 通，梁世起家國子生，舉明經，為祕書郎、太子舍人。

translations.literal: Tong, in Liang times began as National University student, passed the classics examination, and became Secretary and Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang, Tong entered service as a national university student, passed the classics examination, and became secretary and mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 以帝甥封武陽亭侯。

translations.literal: As the emperor's sister's son he was enfeoffed Marquis of Wuyang ting.
translations.idiomatic: As kin of the imperial house he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 累遷王府主簿、限外記室參軍、司徒主簿、太子中庶子、驃騎廬陵王府給事中郎、[3]中權何敬容府長史、給事黃門侍郎，坐事免。

translations.literal: He rose through Chief Clerk in a princely establishment, Extra-Quota Recorder in a commandery staff, Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, Household Supporter of the Heir Apparent, attendant gentleman in the establishment of the Prince of Luling, Grand General of Cavalry, Editorial footnote marker 3. Chief Clerk in the establishment of He Jingrong of Central Authority, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through chief clerk in a princely establishment, extra-quota recorder in a commandery staff, chief clerk in the Ministry of Works, household supporter of the heir apparent, attendant gentleman in the Prince of Luling's establishment, [3] chief clerk to He Jingrong of Central Authority, and attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate, then was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，奔于江陵，元帝以為散騎常侍，遷守太常卿。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled to Jiangling; Emperor Yuan made him Regular Attendant of the Secretariat and promoted him to Minister of Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled to Jiangling; Emperor Yuan made him regular attendant of the Secretariat and then minister of ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 自侯景亂後，臺內宮室，嵭皆焚燼，以通兼起部尚書，歸于京師，專掌繕造。

translations.literal: After Jing's rebellion the palace halls within the capital were all burned to ashes; Tong was made concurrent Master of Works in charge of construction, returned to the capital, and solely managed repairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing's rebellion the palaces within the capital had all been burned to ash; Tong was made concurrent master of works for construction, returned to the capital, and alone directed the rebuilding.

sentences.zh: 江陵陷，敬帝承制以通為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing's provisional regime made Tong Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing's provisional regime made Tong director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 紹泰元年，加侍中，尚書如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was added Palace Attendant, Director unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaotai (555) he was added palace attendant while keeping the directorship.

sentences.zh: 尋為尚書右僕射，吏部如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Director of Personnel unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made right vice director of the Masters of Writing, still heading personnel.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，遷左僕射，侍中如故。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, he was transferred to Left Vice Director, Palace Attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, he was transferred to left vice director, retaining palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 文帝嗣位，領太子少傅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he headed Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he headed tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 天康元年，為翊右將軍、右光祿大夫，量置佐史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiankang he was General Who Assists the Right and Right Grand Master of the Golden Sigil, with aides and clerks as needed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiankang (566) he was made General Who Assists the Right and right grand master of the golden sigil, with aides and clerks as needed.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，號安右將軍，又領南徐州大中正。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, his title was changed to General Who Pacifies the Right, and he again headed Grand Arbiter of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, his title was changed to General Who Pacifies the Right, and he again headed grand arbiter of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，遷左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian he was transferred to Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taijian (569) he was transferred to left grand master of the golden sigil.

sentences.zh: 六年，加特進，侍中、將軍、光祿、佐史嵭如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was given Supernumerary Privilege; Palace Attendant, general, Grand Master, and aides unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was given supernumerary privilege; palace attendant, general, grand master, and aides all remained as before.

sentences.zh: 未拜卒，時年七十二。

translations.literal: Before he took up the appointment he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could enter the new office he died, aged seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 詔贈本官，諡曰成，葬日給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously restored his offices, posthumous name Cheng, and on the burial day granted one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored his offices posthumously, gave him the posthumous name Cheng, and granted one set of martial music on the day of burial.

sentences.zh: 弟質、弟固各有傳。

translations.literal: Younger brothers Zhi and Gu each have a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Zhi and Gu each have a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 勱字公濟，[4]通之弟也。

translations.literal: Mo, styled Gongji, Editorial footnote marker 4. was Tong's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Mo, styled Gongji, [4] was Tong's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 美風儀，博涉書史，恬然清簡，未嘗以利欲干懷。

translations.literal: Fine bearing and deportment, broad learning in books and histories, calmly pure and simple, never had profit or desire tug at his heart.
translations.idiomatic: He had a fine presence, wide reading in history, and a calm, spare manner; profit and desire never touched his mind.

sentences.zh: 梁世為國子周易生，射策舉高第，除祕書郎、太子舍人、宣惠武陵王主簿、輕車河東王功曹史。

translations.literal: In Liang he was a National University student in the Book of Changes, scored highest in the archery-and-writing examination, appointed Secretary, Mentor to the Heir Apparent, personal secretary to the Prince of Wuling of Xuanhui, and Records Officer to the Prince of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he studied the Book of Changes at the national university, took top marks in the archery-and-writing examination, and served as secretary, mentor to the heir apparent, personal secretary to the Prince of Wuling of Xuanhui, and records officer to the Prince of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 王出鎮京口，勱將隨之藩，范陽張纘時典選舉，勱造纘言別，纘嘉其風采，乃曰：「王生才地，豈可游外府乎？

translations.literal: When the prince went out to hold Jiangkou, Mo was about to follow to the principality; Zhang Zuan of Fanyang then held selection offices; Mo went to bid Zuan farewell; Zuan admired his presence and said: "Master Wang's talent and standing—how can he wander in an outer princely house?
translations.idiomatic: When the prince went out to hold Jiangkou, Mo was to accompany him to the fief; Zhang Zuan of Fanyang then controlled appointments. Mo came to take leave of him, and Zuan, struck by his bearing, said, "A man of your talent and station—how can he be left to wander in an outer princely house?

sentences.zh: 」奏為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: " He memorialized to make him Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: " He memorialized to make him grand mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 遷中舍人，司徒左西屬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant to the Heir Apparent and Left Western Adjutant of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was transferred to attendant to the heir apparent and left western adjutant in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 出為南徐州別駕從事史。

translations.literal: He went out as Registrar and Retainer's Assistant of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as registrar and retainer's assistant of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 大同末，梁武帝謁園陵，道出朱方，勱隨例迎候，队勱令從輦側，所經山川，莫不顧問，勱隨事應對，咸有故實。

translations.literal: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs; the route passed through Zhufang; Mo greeted him per custom; the Emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; every mountain and river passed, the Emperor inquired; Mo answered each matter with historical precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs by way of Zhufang; Mo met him as custom required. The emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; at every hill and stream he asked questions, and Mo answered each with historical precedent.

sentences.zh: 又從登北顧樓，賦詩，辭義清典，帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: He also followed him up Beigu Tower to compose poetry; the diction was clear and canonical; the Emperor greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed him up Beigu Tower to compose verse; the language was clear and classical, and the emperor praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 時河東王為廣州刺史，乃以勱為冠軍河東王長史、南海太守。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Hedong was Inspector of Guangzhou; Mo was made Chief Clerk to the Prince of Hedong, Champion, and Administrator of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Hedong was inspector of Guangzhou; Mo was made his chief clerk, champion, and administrator of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 王至嶺南，多所侵掠，因懼罪稱疾，委州還朝，勱行廣州府事。

translations.literal: The prince reached Lingnan and there greatly plundered; fearing guilt he claimed illness, entrusted the province and returned to court; Mo conducted Guangzhou establishment affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The prince reached Lingnan and plundered widely; fearing punishment he pleaded illness, handed back the province, and returned to court, leaving Mo to run Guangzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 越中饒沃，前後守宰例多貪縱，勱獨以清白著聞。

translations.literal: The Yue region was rich; former governors and magistrates were usually greedy and licentious; Mo alone was known for purity and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The Yue country was wealthy, and former governors and magistrates were commonly greedy and unrestrained; Mo alone was known for clean government.

sentences.zh: 入為給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered court as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，西奔江陵，元帝承制以為太子中庶子，掌相府管記。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled west to Jiangling; Emperor Yuan's provisional regime made him Household Supporter of the Heir Apparent, in charge of the chief minister's records.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled west to Jiangling; under Emperor Yuan's provisional regime he was household supporter of the heir apparent, in charge of the chief minister's records.

sentences.zh: 出為寧遠將軍、晉陵太守。

translations.literal: He went out as General of Distant Pacification and Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as General of Distant Pacification and administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 時兵饑之後，郡中凋弊，勱為政清簡，吏民便安之。

translations.literal: After troops and famine the commandery was wasted; Mo's government was pure and simple, and officials and people found ease.
translations.idiomatic: After war and famine the commandery lay in ruins; Mo governed plainly and simply, and officials and people alike were at ease.

sentences.zh: 徵為侍中，遷五兵尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Palace Attendant and promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as palace attendant and promoted to minister of war.

sentences.zh: 及西魏寇江陵，元帝徵湘州刺史宜豐侯蕭循入援，以勱監湘州。

translations.literal: When Western Wei raided Jiangling, Emperor Yuan summoned the Inspector of Xiangzhou, Marquis of Yifeng Xiao Xun, to aid; Mo was left to oversee Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Wei attacked Jiangling, Emperor Yuan summoned Xiao Xun, Marquis of Yifeng and inspector of Xiangzhou, to reinforce him; Mo was left to oversee the province.

sentences.zh: 江陵陷，敬帝承制以為中書令。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing's provisional regime made him Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing's provisional regime made him director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 紹泰元年加侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was added Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaotai he was added palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 高祖為司空，以勱兼司空長史。

translations.literal: When the Founder was Minister of Works, Mo was concurrently Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder was minister of works, Mo was concurrently his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，

translations.literal: When the Founder was Chancellor,
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder was chancellor,

translations.literal: (as)
translations.idiomatic: (as)

sentences.zh: [勱]兼丞相長史，[5]侍中、中書令嵭如故。

translations.literal: [Mo] was concurrently Chief Clerk to the Chancellor, Editorial footnote marker 5. Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was concurrently chief clerk to the chancellor, [5] retaining palace attendant and director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時吳中遭亂，民多乏絕，乃以勱監吳興郡。

translations.literal: At the time Wu suffered disorder and the people were much in want; Mo was made overseer of Wu commandery of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was then in turmoil and the people were destitute; Mo was put in charge of Wu commandery of Xing.

sentences.zh: 及蕭勃平後，又以勱舊在嶺表，早有政勣，乃授使持節、都督廣州等二十州諸軍事、平南將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: After Xiao Bo was pacified, because Mo had long been in Lingnan with earlier administrative merit, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander over twenty prefectures including Guangzhou, General Who Pacifies the South, General of the Pacification of Yue Central Corps, and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Bo was subdued, because Mo had long served in Lingnan with a record of good rule, he was given the staff, command over twenty prefectures including Guangzhou, the titles General Who Pacifies the South and General of the Pacification of Yue Central Corps, and the post of inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，改為衡州刺史，持節、都督嵭如故。

translations.literal: Before he set out, he was changed to Inspector of Hengzhou, staff and command unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post he was reassigned to inspector of Hengzhou, with staff and command unchanged.

sentences.zh: 王琳據有上流，衡、廣攜貳，勱不得之鎮，留于大庾嶺。

translations.literal: Wang Lin held the upper reaches; Heng and Guang wavered; Mo could not reach his post and remained at Dayu Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi; Heng and Guang were divided in loyalty; Mo could not reach his command and stayed at Dayu Ridge.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，徵為侍中、都官尚書，未拜，復為中書令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of the Masters of Writing for Capital Offenses, but before taking office he was again made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year one he was called up as attendant-in-ordinary and minister of capital offenses, but before he took up the post he was again made director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷太子詹事，行東宮事，侍中嵭如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Tutor to the Crown Prince, acting administrator of the Eastern Palace, his post as Attendant-in-Ordinary unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was made tutor to the crown prince and acting head of the eastern palace, keeping his attendant-in-ordinary rank.

sentences.zh: 加金紫光祿大夫，領度支尚書。

translations.literal: He was given the rank of Grandee with the Golden Horse and Grand Seal and concurrently held the post of Director of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grandee with the golden horse seal and also directed the revenue office.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was given the additional title of Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant as well.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing (right).
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year one he was made right vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 時東境大水，百姓饑饉，以勱為仁武將軍、晉陵太守。

translations.literal: At that time the eastern regions suffered great floods and the people were in famine; Mo was made General of Benevolent Martial Might and Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: The east was then stricken by flood and famine, and Mo was sent out as benevolent-martial general and administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 在郡甚有威惠，郡人表請立碑，頌勱政績，詔許之。

translations.literal: In the commandery he had great authority and kindness; the people of the commandery memorialized requesting a stele to praise Mo's achievements, and an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Jinling with real authority and kindness; the people petitioned for a stele to his record and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 徵為中書監，重授尚書右僕射，領右軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Supervisor of the Secretariat, again appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing (right), and concurrently Right Army General.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as supervisor of the secretariat, again made right vice director of the masters of writing, and given the right army generalship.

sentences.zh: 四年五月卒，時年六十七。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of year four, at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、中書監，諡曰溫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Supervisor of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made attendant-in-ordinary and supervisor of the secretariat, with the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 袁敬字子恭，陳郡陽夏人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Jing, courtesy name Zigong, was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jing, styled Zigong, was from Yangxia in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖顗，宋侍中、吏部尚書、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan was a Song Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Personnel, and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan had been a Song attendant-in-ordinary, minister of personnel, and inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 父昂，梁侍中、司空，諡穆公。

translations.literal: His father Ang was a Liang Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Duke Mu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ang had been a Liang attendant-in-ordinary and minister of works, posthumously Duke Mu.

sentences.zh: 樞字踐言，梁吳郡太守君正之子也。

translations.literal: Shu, courtesy name Jianyan, was the son of Junzheng, Administrator of Wu commandery under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, styled Jianyan, was the son of Junzheng, Liang's administrator of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 美容儀，性沈靜，好讀書，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: He had fine looks and a calm disposition, loved reading, and never put down his books.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome and reserved, loved books, and always had one in hand.

sentences.zh: 家世顯貴，貲產充積，而樞獨居處率素，傍無交往，端坐一室，非公事未嘗出遊，榮利之懷淡如也。

translations.literal: His family for generations had been illustrious and wealthy, yet Shu alone lived plainly; he had no companions at his side, sat upright in a single room, and unless on public business never went abroad—his heart toward glory and profit was utterly indifferent.
translations.idiomatic: Though his house was great and rich, Shu lived simply alone, kept no company, and sat in one room; he went out only on duty and cared nothing for rank or gain.

sentences.zh: 起家梁祕書郎，歷太子舍人，輕車河東王主簿，安前邵陵王、中軍宣

translations.literal: He first entered office as a Liang Secretariat Gentleman, then served as Aide to the Crown Prince, Registrar to the Prince of Hedong of the Light Chariots, and Merit Clerk in the two prefectures of the preceding Prince of Shaoling and the Central Army Prince Xuan
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Liang secretariat gentleman, then served as crown prince aide, registrar to the prince of Hedong of the light chariots, and merit clerk in the households of the former prince of Shaoling and the central army prince Xuan

translations.literal: (Cheng)
translations.idiomatic: (Cheng)

sentences.zh: [城]王二府功曹史。

translations.literal: [City] Wang.
translations.idiomatic: [City] Wang.

sentences.zh: [6]侯景之亂，樞往吳郡省父，因丁父憂。

translations.literal: [6] During Hou Jing's rebellion Shu went to Wu commandery to visit his father and thereupon entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: [6] In Hou Jing's rebellion Shu went to Wu commandery to see his father and then mourned his father's death.

sentences.zh: 時四方擾亂，人求苟免，樞居喪以至孝聞。

translations.literal: At the time the four quarters were in turmoil and men sought only to escape harm; Shu's conduct in mourning became known for supreme filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was in chaos and men sought only to save themselves, but Shu's mourning won fame for deep filial piety.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯平侯景，鎮京城，衣冠爭往造請，樞獨杜門靜居，不求聞達。

translations.literal: When Wang Sengbian pacified Hou Jing and held the capital, the gentry all rushed to call on him; Shu alone shut his doors and lived quietly, seeking no fame.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian took the capital after defeating Hou Jing, the elite flocked to him; Shu stayed indoors and sought no advancement.

sentences.zh: 紹泰元年，徵為給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was summoned as Supernumerary Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaotai year one he was summoned as supernumerary attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 未拜，除員外散騎常侍，兼侍中。

translations.literal: Before he took office he was appointed Outer Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, concurrently Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up the post he was made outer scattered-cavalry regular attendant and attendant-in-ordinary at the same time.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he concurrently held the post of Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he also served as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 其年出為吳興太守。

translations.literal: That year he went out as Administrator of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was posted as administrator of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，徵為左民尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongding he was summoned as Left Minister for the People.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year two he was summoned as left minister for the people.

sentences.zh: 未至，改侍中，掌大選事。

translations.literal: Before he arrived he was changed to Attendant-in-Ordinary and put in charge of the great selections.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up that post he was made attendant-in-ordinary and put in charge of high appointments.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷都官尚書，掌選如故。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Minister of the Masters of Writing for Capital Offenses, with charge of selections as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he was made minister of capital offenses, still overseeing appointments.

sentences.zh: 樞博聞彊識，明悉舊章。

translations.literal: Shu was broadly learned with a strong memory and clearly understood old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was widely read, had a strong memory, and knew the old rules well.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖長女永世公主先適陳留太守錢蕆，生子岊，[7]主及岊嵭卒于梁世。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Founder's eldest daughter, Princess Yongshi, had first been married to Qian Yi, Administrator of Chenliu, and bore a son Jie; [7] the princess and Jie had both died in the Liang era.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Founder's eldest daughter, Princess Yongshi, had married Qian Yi, administrator of Chenliu, and borne a son Jie; [7] both princess and son had died under Liang.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，唯公主追封。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, only the princess was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, only the princess received a posthumous enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 至是將葬，尚書主客請詳議，欲加蕆駙馬都尉，并贈岊官。

translations.literal: At this time she was about to be buried; the Host-Guests Office of the Masters of Writing requested detailed deliberation, wishing to add Yi as Commandant of the Consort's Carriage and also to bestow an office on Jie.
translations.idiomatic: As burial approached, the host-guests office of the masters of writing asked for a full ruling, proposing to make Yi commandant of the consort's carriage and to grant Jie an office as well.

sentences.zh: 樞議曰：「昔王姬下嫁，必適諸侯，同姓為主，[8]聞於公羊之說，車服不繫，顯於詩人之篇。

translations.literal: Shu argued: "In antiquity when a king's daughter married down, she was always given to a feudal lord; that the chief wife be of the same surname [8] is heard in the Gongyang tradition, and that chariots and dress not be tied to rank is plain in the poets' odes.
translations.idiomatic: Shu argued: "Anciently a king's daughter married down only to feudal lords; that the chief wife share the surname [8] is in the Gongyang school, and that carriage and dress not be bound to rank appears in the Odes.

sentences.zh: 漢氏初興，列侯尚主，自斯以後，降嬪素族。

translations.literal: When the Han house first rose, marquises married imperial daughters; from then on princesses were married down to plain clans.
translations.idiomatic: At Han's rise marquises married imperial daughters; afterward princesses wed common families.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉置由漢武，[9]或以假諸功臣，或以加於戚屬，是以魏曹植表駙馬、奉車趣為一號。

translations.literal: The post of Commandant of the Consort's Carriage was established by Emperor Wu of Han; [9] sometimes it was lent to meritorious ministers, sometimes added for kin—hence in Wei, Cao Zhi petitioned to make the consort commandant and the carriage attendant a single title.
translations.idiomatic: The consort commandant was created by Han Wudi; [9] it was sometimes given to meritorious ministers and sometimes to kin—hence Cao Zhi in Wei asked to merge consort commandant and carriage attendant into one title.

sentences.zh: 齊職儀曰，凡尚公主必拜駙馬都尉，魏、晉以來，因為瞻準。

translations.literal: The Qi Regulations of Offices say that whoever marries a princess must receive the title Commandant of the Consort's Carriage; from Wei and Jin onward this became the standard.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi office regulations say that a princess's husband must be made consort commandant; from Wei and Jin on that was the rule.

sentences.zh: 蓋以王姬之重，庶姓之輕，若不加其等級，寧可合劜而酳，所以假駙馬之位，乃崇於皇女也。

translations.literal: This was because the king's daughter is weighty and a common surname is light: if her husband's rank were not raised, how could they share the cup and drink together? Hence the borrowed post of consort commandant was meant to honor the imperial daughter.
translations.idiomatic: A king's daughter outranked a common house; without raising the husband's rank they could not share the marriage cup—so the consort commandant honored the princess.

sentences.zh: 今公主早薨，伉儷已絕，既無禮數致疑，何須駙馬之授？

translations.literal: Now the princess died early and the marriage bond is severed; since no ritual question remains, why is the consort commandant needed?
translations.idiomatic: The princess is long dead and the marriage ended; with no ritual issue left, why grant a consort commandant?

sentences.zh: 案杜預尚晉宣帝第二女高陵宣公主，晉武踐祚，而主已亡，泰始中追贈公主，元凱無復駙馬之號。

translations.literal: Consider Du Yu, who married the second daughter of Jin's Emperor Xuan, Princess Gao Ling Xuan; when Jin's Emperor Wu took the throne the princess was already dead, and in the Taishi era she was posthumously enfeoffed as princess—Yu received no consort commandant title.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu married Jin Xuandi's second daughter, Princess Gao Ling Xuan; when Jin Wudi came to the throne she was already dead, and though she was enfeoffed posthumously in Taishi, Yu was never called consort commandant.

sentences.zh: 梁

translations.literal: Liang
translations.idiomatic: Liang

translations.literal: (zhi)
translations.idiomatic: (zhi)

sentences.zh: [文]帝女新安穆公主早薨，[10]天監初王氏無追拜之事。

translations.literal: [Wen] Emperor's daughter, Princess Xin'an Mu, died early; [10] at the beginning of Tianjian the Wang clan received no retrospective appointment.
translations.idiomatic: [Wen] Emperor's daughter Princess Xin'an Mu died young; [10] at the start of Tianjian the Wangs were given no retrospective title.

sentences.zh: 遠近二例，足以據明。

translations.literal: These two precedents, near and far, suffice as proof.
translations.idiomatic: These two cases, ancient and recent, are proof enough.

sentences.zh: 公主所生，既未及成人之禮，無勞此授，今宜追贈亭侯。

translations.literal: The princess's son had not yet reached the rites of adulthood, so this appointment is needless; now he should be posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Ting.
translations.idiomatic: The princess's son had not reached adulthood and needs no such title; he should be enfeoffed posthumously as marquis of ting.

sentences.zh: 」時以樞議為長。

translations.literal: " At the time Shu's argument was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " The court followed Shu's opinion.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，守吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia he acted as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year one he acted as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 三年，即真。

translations.literal: In the third year he was confirmed in the post.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he was confirmed in office.

sentences.zh: 尋領右軍將軍，又領丹陽尹，本官如故。

translations.literal: Soon he concurrently held the post of Right Army General and also served as Intendant of Danyang, his original posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He soon added right army general and intendant of Danyang, keeping his other posts.

sentences.zh: 五年，以葬父，拜表自解，詔賜絹布五十匹，錢十萬，令葬訖停宅視郡事，

translations.literal: In the fifth year, because he was burying his father, he submitted a memorial resigning his posts; an edict granted fifty bolts of silk and a hundred thousand cash and ordered that after the burial he remain at home overseeing commandery affairs,
translations.idiomatic: In year five, while burying his father, he asked to resign; the court gave fifty bolts of silk and a hundred thousand cash and told him to stay home after the funeral and still oversee commandery business,

translations.literal: (burial)
translations.idiomatic: (burial)

sentences.zh: 服闋，[11]還復本職。

translations.literal: and when mourning ended [11] he returned to his original posts.
translations.idiomatic: and when mourning ended [11] he resumed his former offices.

sentences.zh: 其年秩滿，解尹，加散騎常侍，將軍、尚書嵭如故。

translations.literal: That year his term ended; he was relieved of the intendant post and given Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant; his generalship and ministership remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he left the intendant post, was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and kept his generalship and ministry.

sentences.zh: 是時，僕射到仲舉雖參掌選事，銓衡汲引，嵭出於樞，其所舉薦，多會上旨。

translations.literal: At that time the Vice Director Dao Zhongju, though he shared in selections, the weighing and promotion largely came from Shu; his recommendations mostly matched the sovereign's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Though Vice Director Dao Zhongju shared appointments, Shu largely controlled selection and his nominees usually pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 謹慎周密，清白自居，文武職司，鮮有遊其門者。

translations.literal: Careful and thorough, he kept himself pure; civil and military officials rarely visited his door.
translations.idiomatic: Careful, discreet, and upright, he had few visitors from office, civil or military.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，遷尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing (left).
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne he was made left vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 光大元年卒，時年五十一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangda he died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Guangda year one, at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、左光祿大夫，諡曰簡懿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Grandee with the Glorious Credentials, with the posthumous name Jianyi.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made attendant-in-ordinary and left grandee with glorious credentials, with the posthumous name Jianyi.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷行於世。

translations.literal: A collection of ten juan circulated in his day.
translations.idiomatic: A collection in ten juan circulated in his lifetime.

sentences.zh: 弟憲自有傳。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xian has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xian has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：王沖、王通嵭以貴游早升清貫，而允蹈禮節，篤誠奉上，斯為美焉。

translations.literal: The historian says: Wang Chong and Wang Tong, as scions of noble houses, early rose to pure office, yet faithfully observed ritual and served the throne with deep sincerity—this is admirable.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Wang Chong and Wang Tong, born to privilege and early raised to high office, still kept the rites and served faithfully—here is what deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 王勱之襟神夷澹，袁樞之端操沉冥，雖拘放為異，而勝躯一揆，古所謂名士者，蓋在其人乎！

translations.literal: Wang Mo's spirit was calm and detached; Yuan Shu's integrity was deep and hidden; though restraint and release differed in form, their excellence was of one measure—the famed gentlemen of old, were they not such men as these?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mo's mind was serene and Yuan Shu's conduct grave; one held back and one withdrew, yet both excelled alike—the "eminent men" of antiquity were surely such as these.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 以帝甥賜爵安東亭侯 「安東」《南史》作「東安」。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed as Marquis of Andong ting because he was the emperor's nephew-by-marriage—"Andong" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Dongan."
translations.idiomatic: On "enfeoffed as marquis of Andong ting as the emperor's nephew": the Southern Dynasties history reads Dongan.

sentences.zh: 父琳司徒左長史 「司徒」北監本、汲本、殿本作「司空」。

translations.literal: Father Lin, Chief Clerk of the Director of the Masters of Works—"Director of the Masters of Works" in the Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions reads "Minister of Works."
translations.idiomatic: On "father Lin, chief clerk of the director of the masters of works": Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions read minister of works.

sentences.zh: 按錢大昕《廿二史考異》云此別一王琳。

translations.literal: According to Qian Daxin's Examination of the Twenty-Two Histories, this is a different Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Daxin's Examination of the Twenty-Two Histories notes that this is a different Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 驃騎廬陵王府給事中郎 張森楷

translations.literal: Rapid Cavalry Prince of Luling's mansion Giver-in-Attendant—Zhang Senkai
translations.idiomatic: Rapid Cavalry Prince of Luling's mansion giver-in-attendant—Zhang Senkai

sentences.zh: 〈校勘記〉

translations.literal: 〈Collation notes〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Collation notes〉

sentences.zh: 云：「『給』疑當作『從』，官志無給事中郎。」

translations.literal: says: "'Giver' is suspect and should read 'follow'; the office regulations have no giver-in-attendant."
translations.idiomatic: writes: "'Giver' is probably 'follow'; the office list has no giver-in-attendant."

sentences.zh: 勱字公濟 「公濟」《南史》、《元龜》六七二作「公齊」。

translations.literal: Mo, courtesy name Gongji—"Gongji" in the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Imperial Mirror 672 reads "Gongqi."
translations.idiomatic: On "Mo styled Gongji": the Southern Dynasties history and Imperial Mirror 672 read Gongqi.

translations.literal: (wei)
translations.idiomatic: (wei)

sentences.zh: [勱]兼丞相長史 據北監本、汲本、殿本改。

translations.literal: [Mo] concurrently Chief Clerk of the Chancellor—changed according to the Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "[Mo] concurrently chief clerk of the chancellor": emended per Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions.

sentences.zh: 安前邵陵王中軍宣

translations.literal: Preceding Prince of Shaoling, Central Army Prince Xuan
translations.idiomatic: Preceding prince of Shaoling, central army prince Xuan

translations.literal: (Cheng)
translations.idiomatic: (Cheng)

sentences.zh: [城]王二府功曹史 張森楷

translations.literal: [City] Wang, merit clerk in two prefectures—Zhang Senkai
translations.idiomatic: [City] Wang, two prefectures' merit clerk—Zhang Senkai

sentences.zh: 〈校勘記〉

translations.literal: 〈Collation notes〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Collation notes〉

sentences.zh: 云：「『成』當作『城』，梁無宣成王。

translations.literal: says: "'Cheng' should read 'city'; Liang had no Prince Xuan Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: writes: "'Cheng' should be 'city'; Liang had no Prince Xuan Cheng.

sentences.zh: 」按梁簡文帝長子大器封宣城郡王，見《梁書·哀太子傳》。

translations.literal: " According to the Biography of the Lamented Crown Prince in the Book of Liang, the eldest son of Emperor Jianwen, Daqi, was enfeoffed as Prince of Xuancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Liang's biography of the lamented crown prince shows Jianwen's eldest son Daqi enfeoffed as prince of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 張說是，今據改。

translations.literal: Zhang's view is correct; the text is now changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang is right; the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 生子岊 「岊」原訛「𡵒」，各本不訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Bore a son Jie—"Jie" was originally corrupt as another character; the other editions are not corrupt; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "bore a son Jie": the character was corrupt in the base text; other editions read correctly—now fixed.

sentences.zh: 下同。

translations.literal: The same below.
translations.idiomatic: The same below.

sentences.zh: 同姓為主 「主」原訛「王」，今據北監本、汲本、殿本改正。

translations.literal: Same surname as chief—"chief" was originally corrupt as "king"; now corrected according to the Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "same surname as chief": zhu was corrupt as wang—emended per Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions.

sentences.zh: 按語本《公羊莊元年傳》。

translations.literal: According to the source, this phrase comes from the Gongyang, Duke Zhuang year one.
translations.idiomatic: The line comes from the Gongyang commentary, Duke Zhuang year one.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉置由漢武 「由」字原本漫漶，今據各本補。

translations.literal: The post of Commandant of the Consort's Carriage was established by Emperor Wu of Han—the character "by" in the original was effaced; it is now supplied from the various editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "consort commandant established by Han Wudi": the character you was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.

sentences.zh: 梁

translations.literal: Liang
translations.idiomatic: Liang

translations.literal: (zhi)
translations.idiomatic: (zhi)

sentences.zh: [文]帝女新安穆公主早薨 據《南史》改。

translations.literal: [Wen] Emperor's daughter, Princess Xin'an Mu, died early—changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: On "[Wen] Emperor's daughter Princess Xin'an Mu died early": emended per the Southern Dynasties history.

sentences.zh: 按梁武帝即位後，追尊其父為文皇帝。

translations.literal: According to the note, after Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne he posthumously honored his father as Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang Wudi's accession he honored his father posthumously as Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 王沖傳言其母為梁武帝妹新安穆公主，與此合。

translations.literal: The biography of Wang Chong says his mother was Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess Xin'an Mu—this agrees.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong's biography says his mother was Liang Wudi's sister Princess Xin'an Mu, which matches.

sentences.zh: 作「文」是。

translations.literal: To write "Wen" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Wen is the correct reading.

translations.literal: (burial)
translations.idiomatic: (burial)

sentences.zh: 服闋 據《南史》刪。

translations.literal: When mourning ended—deleted according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: On "when mourning ended": omitted per the Southern Dynasties history.
